findings.title: Shared SSLContext mutated by load_cert_chain leaks client certs process-wide
findings.suggested_fix: Do not hand out the shared context when anything else in the pool will mutate it. Minimal: in _urllib3_request_context only use the preloaded context when client_cert is None, i.e. `elif verify is True: if client_cert is None: pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context else: pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` (restoring per-connection behavior for mTLS). If mTLS should also be cached, keep a dict of contexts keyed by (cert_file, key_file), each built with create_urllib3_context() + load_verify_locations(default bundle) + load_cert_chain(...), never shared across different client-cert tuples.

findings.title: Injected ssl_context overrides TLS settings from init_poolmanager subclasses
findings.suggested_fix: Only inject the preloaded context when the target manager has no TLS configuration of its own. In _get_connection, after selecting `manager` (self.poolmanager or the proxy manager): `if pool_kwargs.get("ssl_context") is _preloaded_ssl_context and any(k in manager.connection_pool_kw for k in ("ssl_context", "ssl_version", "ssl_minimum_version", "ssl_maximum_version", "ca_certs", "ca_cert_dir", "ca_cert_data")): del pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]; pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` so such adapters keep the pre-change behavior.
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:400-402: `conn = self.poolmanager.connection_from_host(**host_params, pool_kwargs=pool_kwargs)` with pool_kwargs containing `"ssl_context": _preloaded_ssl_context` (adapters.py:95); urllib3 poolmanager.py:409 `base_pool_kwargs[key] = value` lets it override connection_pool_kw

findings.title: verify=True no longer sets ca_certs; HTTPS proxy leg verifies with OS store
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the certifi bundle attached to connections that will not use the shared context: in _get_connection, when the selected proxy scheme is https and verify is True, add `pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` alongside ssl_context (only the proxy leg then calls load_verify_locations). For the legacy hook, in cert_verify set `conn.ca_certs = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` when `verify is True` and `getattr(conn, "conn_kw", {}).get("ssl_context") is None`.

findings.title: CA bundle now loaded at import; missing bundle breaks `import requests`
findings.suggested_fix: Build the context lazily and defensively via a cached accessor (`_get_preloaded_ssl_context()` under a threading.Lock) called from the `verify is True` branch of _urllib3_request_context; check `os.path.exists(cert_loc)` first and raise the pre-change descriptive OSError('Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: ...') instead of failing at import.

residual_risks: Shared-context mutation beyond client certs: a subclass passing assert_hostname/assert_fingerprint via init_poolmanager makes urllib3 set check_hostname=False on the module-level context process-wide; urllib3 falls back to its own _match_hostname so hostname verification is preserved, but the global change is irreversible and was not traced under pyOpenSSL injection performed after `import requests`.

residual_risks: Shared-context mutations other than load_cert_chain/load_verify_locations/verify_mode were traced but not flagged: urllib3 sets `check_hostname = False` on the shared context whenever any pool uses assert_hostname/assert_fingerprint or pyOpenSSL is injected (connection.py:1045-1056); this is persistent but urllib3's `_match_hostname` fallback (connection.py:1098-1119) still verifies hostnames for later connections, so no verification bypass was constructible. It does mean the shared context's check_hostname state depends on which adapter ran first in the process.

pyOpenSSL (`urllib3.contrib.pyopenssl.inject_into_urllib3`) is not installed here, so two behaviours were reasoned from source only: injecting after `import requests` leaves `_preloaded_ssl_context` as a stdlib context (verify=True then bypasses pyOpenSSL entirely), and `PyOpenSSLContext.verify_mode` has no check_hostname guard, which would turn the http-via-https-proxy ValueError into a silent CERT_NONE flip of the shared context racing concurrent verify=True handshakes.

residual_risks: Shared-state correctness (owned by correctness/security reviewers, evidence supplied for routing): with verify=True and cert=(certfile, keyfile), urllib3/util/ssl_.py:429-433 calls `context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)` on the process-wide `_preloaded_ssl_context` per connection (verified offline: {'load_cert_chain [shared]': 3}); the client certificate then remains loaded in the context used by every other verify=True pool, session and thread in the process.

Behavioral regression (owned by correctness reviewer, evidence supplied for routing): urllib3 poolmanager.py:400-409 `_merge_pool_kwargs` lets request-level pool_kwargs override PoolManager-level kwargs, so an HTTPAdapter subclass that injects `ssl_context=custom` via init_poolmanager (documented pattern for truststore / custom TLS) silently has its context replaced by `_preloaded_ssl_context` on every verify=True request (verified offline: pool.conn_kw['ssl_context'] is custom -> False, is _preloaded -> True; verify=False keeps the custom context). At base, pool_kwargs carried only cert_reqs so the custom context survived.

HTTPS-proxy (CONNECT tunnel) path: urllib3/connection.py:964-967 `_connect_tls_proxy` uses `ssl_context = None` and `ca_certs = self.ca_certs` for tunneling proxies; since cert_verify no longer sets ca_certs for verify=True, the proxy leg now falls through to `load_default_certs()` (OS trust store) on a fresh context per connection instead of certifi's bundle. Per-connection CA loading still happens on this path (not a perf regression; load_default_certs measured ~0.2 ms on this Linux host) but the trust store used to verify the proxy changes -- a correctness/security matter for other reviewers.

Import-time cost checked and judged immaterial: module-level create_urllib3_context()+load_verify_locations(certifi bundle, 240 KB) costs ~3 ms once per process (`import requests` total ~52 ms; adapters self-time 4.7 ms under -X importtime). Not reported as a finding. A missing/unreadable DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH now fails at `import requests` rather than at first HTTPS request (correctness lane).
testing_gaps: No test asserts the performance invariant the PR exists for: that a verify=True HTTPS pool from HTTPAdapter._get_connection carries `conn_kw['ssl_context'] is adapters._preloaded_ssl_context` with ca_certs/ca_cert_dir None, and that repeated requests to the same host reuse one pool; a monkeypatched ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations counter around two connections would lock in the zero-per-connection behavior.
